title: [YouPass Collect] - Student course enrollment trends across three decades
prompt: The pie charts below show the different types of courses, which were followed by the students during the years of 1984, 1994 and 2004. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the proportions of students enrolled in four different types of courses across three separate years: 1984, 1994, and 2004.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the data reveal a significant shift in student preferences over the three-decade period, with traditional face-to-face instruction experiencing a substantial decline while alternative learning methods, particularly mixed media courses, gained considerable popularity. Despite these changes, face-to-face courses remained the most common format throughout the entire period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the categories that experienced downward trends, in 1984, face-to-face courses dominated the educational landscape, accounting for 67% of student enrollment, more than three times higher than correspondence courses at 20%. Over the following decade, the proportion of face-to-face learning decreased by 13 percentage points to 54% in 1994, before declining further to 40% by 2004, representing an overall drop of 27 percentage points. Similarly, correspondence courses maintained their share at 20% between 1984 and 1994, but subsequently fell to 15% in the final year, marking a modest decline of 5 percentage points over the entire period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the expanding categories, mixed media courses represented merely 13% of enrollment in 1984, slightly lower than correspondence courses. However, this figure rose marginally to 15% in 1994, before surging dramatically to 35% by 2004, an increase of 22 percentage points overall. Meanwhile, online courses were non-existent in 1984 but emerged in 1994 at 11%, before experiencing a slight decrease to 10% in 2004.
